question: A closed conducting coil of total resistance $R$ is connected as a complete circuit (assume $R$ remains constant) and its self-inductance is negligible. A bar magnet is moved relative to the coil from an initial position to a final position such that the magnetic flux linked with the coil changes from $\Phi_1$ to $\Phi_2$. The same displacement of the magnet is repeated once slowly and once quickly (so the time taken is different, but $\Delta\Phi = \Phi_2-\Phi_1$ is the same). Evaluate the statement: "The total charge flowing through the coil during electromagnetic induction depends on the speed with which the magnet is moved relative to the coil."

options.A: Yes, because higher speed produces a larger induced emf $\varepsilon$ and hence pushes more charge through the circuit.
options.B: No, because the total induced charge depends only on the net change in magnetic flux $\Delta\Phi$ and the (constant) circuit resistance $R$.
options.C: Yes, because charge flow is always $Q = \int I\,dt$, so a faster motion must give a larger $Q$.
options.D: No, because the number of charge carriers in the wire is conserved, so no charge can flow.
